answer.evidence: The stone base is a stepped plinth with a real top surface. The upper tier has top rows 37-40 (L=197, edge line 223 at row 40) and front face rows 41-43 (L=147 down to 118). The lower tier has top rows 44-45, a highlight at row 45, and front rows 46-47. The thin pole (width 2, rows 19-35) has a collar at rows 26-27. At the top, the pole ends in a flat crossbar at rows 5-6 (width 11 over a shaft of 2, about 2 rows). It is a front-facing strip with no ellipse: widths go 4, then 11, then 4, but the bar is a vertical strip with no edge line or eave shadow. The lantern (rows 7-18, width 8) is drawn only as a vertical face with glowing glass, so the lamp head has no top surface. The top end therefore lacks the elliptical cap plate.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a thin iron lamp post with a lantern head, a collar and a stepped stone base, so it matches the prop-lamp-crook reference. It shows 9 visible tones on a full tile and 0% near-flat coverage. The post carries a highlight, mid and dark column, and the base has a light face, a shadow side and a top edge. The 72% near-neutral dark edge share is mixed rather than a pure sticker outline. The reference lamp's own outline is 100% neutral, and neutral dark is natural beside grey iron. The post is thin, as expected for a lamp, but it is not flatter than the reference lamp. The base and lantern add more information than the reference's thin crook. Compared with the richer well and stall, it is simpler, but that is fair for a single thin prop. I see no large flat fills.

Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills.
